extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (library users/developers, computational algebraists) who need reference/usage for the included libraries (customstd.lib, phindex.lib, polybori.lib, autgradalg.lib).
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for selected SINGULAR libraries and procedures (satstd, phindex procedures, PolyBoRi interface, autgradalg functions). Gives usage, assumptions, purpose, notes, theory and examples for each procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: satstd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: satstd(I[,J]); I ideal, J optional ideal. Assume: J generated by variables. Purpose: computes a standard basis of I and, if possible, divides each polynomial during the computation by the variables in J. By default, J is assumed to be the ideal generated by all variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Even if I contains a monomial generated by the variables in J, there is no guarantee that it is found during the computation. If it is found, however, 1 is immediately returned. Note: The result is a standard basis of the saturation wrt. the product of the variables in J. Examples show behaviour: satstd(I,ideal(u,v)) returns unchanged basis; satstd(I,ideal(x)) can return x+1 instead of x^2+x; deg(satstd(I^8)) returns 8 (degree reduction compared to naive std).

rubrics_metrics.name: signatureL
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: signatureL(M[,r]); M symmetric matrix, r int (optional). Return: the signature of M of type int or if r is given and !=0 then intvec with (signature, nr. of +, nr. of -) is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Given matrix M, construct associated quadratic form and use the method of Lagrange to compute signature. The law of inertia (representation as sum of squares) implies signature s = pi - nu where r = pi + nu. The method of Lagrange reduces any real quadratic form to a sum of squares. Reference: Gantmacher, The theory of matrices. Examples: signatureL(M,1) -> 2,3,1; signatureL(H) -> 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: signatureLqf
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: signatureLqf(h); h quadratic form (poly type). Return: the signature of h of type int or if r is given and !=0 then intvec with (signature, nr. of +, nr. of -) is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Same as signatureL but input is a quadratic form polynomial. The method of Lagrange is used; law of inertia described. Examples: signatureLqf(Ax,1) -> 2,3,1; signatureLqf(Bx) -> 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: PH_ais
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: PH_ais(I); I ideal of coordinates of the vector field. Return: the Poincare-Hopf index of type int. Note: the isolated singularity must be algebraically isolated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: For a real analytic vector field X with algebraically isolated singularity at 0, the PH index equals the signature of a non-degenerate bilinear form on the local algebra Qx = R[[x1..xn]]/Ix composed with a linear functional L chosen so that L(Jo)>0, where Jo is residue class of Jacobian determinant. L is defined by expressing Jo in a chosen basis and setting L of the basis element with nonzero coefficient to the sign of that coefficient and other basis elements to 0. Refs: Eisenbud & Levine (1977), Khimshiashvili. Example: PH_ais(I) -> 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: PH_nais
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: PH_nais(I); I ideal of coordinates of the vector field. Return: the Poincare-Hopf index of type int. Note: the vector field must be a non algebraically isolated singularity at 0, with reduced complex zeros of codimension 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: If X = f * Y with f real analytic not changing sign outside 0 and Y having isolated behaviour, let Mx = R[[x]]/(Ix : radical(Ix)) be finite-dimensional subalgebra. The PH index is sign(f) * signature of the non-degenerate bilinear form on Mx composed with a linear functional L chosen so that L(Jp)>0, where Jp is residue class of Jacobian determinant over f^n in Mx. L is defined analogously via basis expansion. Refs: Castellanos-Vargas. Example: PH_nais(I) -> -3.

rubrics_metrics.name: polybori.lib (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: A SINGULAR Library Interface for PolyBoRi. Overview: A library for using PolyBoRi in the SINGULAR interface, with procedures that convert structures (polynomials, rings, ideals) in both directions. Polynomials can be converted to zero-suppressed decision diagrams (zdd) and vice versa. Defines PolyBoRi types bideal, bpoly, bring, and bset for seamless use in SINGULAR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: For using this library SINGULAR's python interface must be available (configure --with-python). To build PolyBoRi you need scons and boost dev libraries. The types implement operations (bpoly: lead, leadmonom, leadcoef; bideal: std, size). Examples demonstrate conversion and use of PolyBoRi boolean groebner basis via boolean_std. See polybori website for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: boolean_std
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: boolean_std(Is); Is ideal. Return: Singular ideal of the boolean groebner basis of Is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: boolean_std(I) returns simplified boolean Groebner basis elements like x(1)+x(4), x(3)+x(4), x(2)+1. For ideals containing 1, result is [1]. Demonstrates behavior over different rings/characteristics; can return monomials like x*z etc. See also conversions to/from bideal for continued PolyBoRi computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: boolean_poly_ring
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure: boolean poly ring (boolean_poly_ring(r)). Purpose: construct a PolyBoRi boolean ring object from the current (or given) SINGULAR ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default: rb == boolean_poly_ring(basering). Optional input rb to override base ring. Examples show creation via pyobject rb = boolean_poly_ring(r) and usage in boolean_constant, boolean_poly, etc. (Section references: D.14.4.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: boolean_constant
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: boolean_constant(const[, rb]); const constant and rb boolean ring. Return: representation of the constant in the boolean ring (pyobject).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: boolean_constant(int(3)) -> 1 (pyobject); boolean_constant(int(0)) -> 0. typeof(boolean_constant(...)) -> pyobject. Optional rb parameter selects boolean ring representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: boolean_poly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: boolean_poly(ps[, dir, rb]); ps polynomial, dir integer zero or one, rb boolean ring. Return: bpoly representation of polynomial ps in PolyBoRi (default representation recursive unless dir==0 for direct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: rb defaults to boolean_poly_ring(basering). The optional dir selects computation method (direct or recursive). Examples: boolean_poly(f) -> polynomial in bpoly form (e.g., x(1)*x(2) + x(2)*x(3) + x(4)*x(5)). boolean_poly(0) -> 0; boolean_poly(1) -> 1. See also direct_boolean_poly and recursive_boolean_poly.

rubrics_metrics.name: direct_boolean_poly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: direct_boolean_poly(f[, rb]); ps polynomial (f), rb boolean ring. Return: direct conversion of polynomial to boolean polynomial (bpoly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show direct_boolean_poly(f) often returning simplified linear forms in boolean context (e.g., x(1) + x(4) or x + 1 depending on ring). Works across rings with different characteristics and returns expected boolean simplifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: recursive_boolean_poly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: recursive_boolean_poly(f[, rb]); ps polynomial (f), rb boolean ring. Return: recursive conversion of polynomial to bpoly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default representation is recursive. Examples mirror direct_boolean_poly outputs; recursive_boolean_poly(f,br2) and recursive_boolean_poly(f,bbr2) both shown. Use when recursive representation is desired or default.

rubrics_metrics.name: boolean_ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: boolean_ideal(Is[, rb]); Is Ideal, rb boolean ring. Return: boolean ideal representation (bideal) of Is in PolyBoRi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default rb == boolean_poly_ring(basering). Examples: boolean_ideal(I) returns list of boolean generators (e.g., x(1) + x(4), x(1)*x(3) + x(1), x(2) + 1, ...). Cases show output with trivial or unit elements ([1]) when ideal contains constants. See also boolean_std, from_boolean_ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: boolean_set
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: boolean_set(ss[, rb]); ss zdd, rb boolean ring. Return: boolean set representation of zdd in ring rb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default: returns boolean set ss in representation of PolyBoRi boolean set in ring rb (boolean_poly_ring). Examples convert polynomials like (x+1)*(y+1)*(z+1) to set of subsets and show full enumerations. See also poly2zdd, from_boolean_set.

rubrics_metrics.name: from_boolean_constant
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: from_boolean_constant(pb); pb pyobject (boolean constant). Return: constant polynomial in Singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: from_boolean_constant(0) -> 0; from_boolean_constant(1) -> 1; from_boolean_constant(pp) -> 1 for a bpoly representing 1. Used to convert boolean constants back to Singular polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: from_boolean_poly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: from_boolean_poly(ps[, dir]); ps boolean polynomial (bpoly), dir integer (0 direct, 1 recursive). Return: polynomial ps in the representation of the boolean ring converted back to Singular polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default method is direct; dir optional to select recursive. Examples: from_boolean_poly(pp) -> x+z; from_boolean_poly(pp,1) -> x+z. Demonstrates conversion across coefficient rings; result consistent with boolean simplification rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: direct_from_boolean_poly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: direct_from_boolean_poly(pb); pb boolean polynomial. Return: polynomial in Singular (direct conversion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: direct_from_boolean_poly(pp) -> x+z; direct_from_boolean_poly(0) -> 0. Use when direct conversion method is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: recursive_from_boolean_poly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: recursive_from_boolean_poly(pb); pb boolean polynomial. Return: polynomial in Singular converted using recursive method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: recursive_from_boolean_poly(pp) -> xy+x+z for certain inputs. Useful when recursive reconstruction yields a different (e.g. sparser) polynomial representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: from_boolean_ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: from_boolean_ideal(Ib); Ib boolean ideal (bideal). Return: ideal in Singular converted from PolyBoRi boolean ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: from_boolean_ideal(Ib) returns Singular ideal generators in standard polynomial form (e.g., x+z, x+y, ...). Works across coefficient rings; multiple examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: from_boolean_set
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: from_boolean_set(fs); fs boolean set (bset). Return: Boolean set sb in representation of a zdd (zero-suppressed decision diagram).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: from_boolean_set(hs) returns zdd textual representation. Demonstrates conversion from PolyBoRi set representation back to SINGULAR's zdd string form. Use when interoperability with zdd-based utilities is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: bvar
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: bvar(i); int i. Return: i-th variable of Boolean ring corresponding to current basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: with ring r = 2,(x,y,z),Dp; bvar(1) -> x. Use to construct boolean variables that correspond to SINGULAR ring variables in PolyBoRi context.

rubrics_metrics.name: poly2zdd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: poly2zdd(poly ps); polynomial ps. Return: polynomial ps in zdd representation (zero-suppressed decision diagram).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: poly2zdd(f) returns zdd textual structure for polynomial f; poly2zdd(x(3)) -> zdd: x3. Use for compact boolean-set style representation and for subsequent zdd operations or disp_zdd visualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: zdd2poly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: zdd2poly(ss); zero-suppressed decision diagram ss. Return: zdd ss in polynomial representation (Singular polynomial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: zdd2poly(poly2zdd(f)) reconstructs polynomial as sum of monomials. zdd2poly(poly2zdd(0)) -> 0; zdd2poly(poly2zdd(1)) -> 1. Use to convert zdd results back to standard polynomial form.

rubrics_metrics.name: disp_zdd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: disp_zdd(ss); zero-suppressed decision diagram ss. Return: string containing visualization of ss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The resulting string is a visualization of the polynomial corresponding to ss with additional zdd structure: every reached else-branch induces a new line. Examples demonstrate multi-line structured visualizations for zdd representations of polynomials. Use for debugging/inspection of zdd structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: autKS
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: autKS(TOR); TOR: optional list of elementary divisors in case of torsion. Assume: the basering is multigraded having used the command setBaseMultigrading(Q) from multigrading.lib. Purpose: Compute the subgroup Aut_K(S) of GL(n) of graded automorphisms of the polynomial ring S (the basering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: returns a ring S and exports an ideal Iexported in the coordinate ring S = K[Y_ij] of GL(n) such that Aut_K(S) = V(I). Notes: Example workflows show attaching degree matrix via setBaseMultigrading(Q), requirements on basering coefficients (QQ), and interacting with exported ideals and variable weights. Requires prior load of gfanlib.so (user must execute LIB 'gfanlib.so' before using this library). Examples illustrate large exported ideals and how to inspect Iexported and variable weights. Use in graded automorphism computations for pointed multigraded rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: autGradAlg
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: autGradAlg(I, TOR); I is an ideal, TOR is an optional list of integers representing the torsion part of the grading group. Assume: minimally presented, degrees of the generators of I are the minimal degrees, basering multigraded pointedly, I_w = 0 for all w = deg(var(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a ring. Also exports an ideal Jexported and a list stabExported. Purpose: compute automorphism group data for graded algebras; examples show typical command sequences (setBaseMultigrading, define I, call autGradAlg) and then inspecting 'resulting ideal' Jexported. Useful for computation of automorphism groups of pointedly graded algebras and Cox ring-based computations for Mori dream spaces.
